root_cause_criterion.criterion: In the `res == 0` branch, after `const Direction dir = _unitIjkToDigit(ijk);`, `localIjkToCell()` must reject `dir == INVALID_DIGIT` before `_getBaseCellNeighbor(originBaseCell, dir)` executes.
root_cause_criterion.description: The vulnerable resolution-0 path computes `dir` from `ijk` and forwards it straight into the base-cell neighbor lookup without checking for `INVALID_DIGIT`. The fixed program adds that missing guard at the same source site.
root_cause_criterion.verification_note: Original vulnerable case: violated (`dir=7`, `basecell_neighbor_call` executed). Original fixed case: guarded (`dir=7`, no protected lookup event). Genuine witness case: `zero_ij_same_origin` (`dir=0`, protected lookup executed on the fixed side).

nodes.state: At `_getBaseCellNeighbor()`, the `dir` parameter used in `baseCellNeighbors[baseCell][dir]` is the same out-of-range direction computed in the res-0 path, so the lookup uses column 7 instead of the valid `0..6` range.

edges.relation: The `dir` value produced by `_unitIjkToDigit(ijk)` in the resolution-0 branch is passed unchanged into `_getBaseCellNeighbor()` as its `dir` parameter, so the sink uses the same invalid direction that the missing guard should have rejected.
